title: RadNet cites study modeling 18.9% fewer prostate biopsies with AI
key_facts: RadNet's DeepHealth unit issued a release on 8 Oct 2026 citing a study published in European Radiology on 26 Sep.

In a retrospective simulation using MRI scans from 2014 to 2025 in Germany, the Netherlands and the US, adding an AI risk score to radiologists' readings of equivocal PI-RADS 3 scans would have avoided 149 biopsies among 787 men (18.9%) while keeping 98.4% sensitivity for clinically significant cancer.
Patient-level sensitivity of the AI classification was 97.6% against 92.6% for PI-RADS (noninferiority met); lesion-level it was 78.8% against 88.8% (noninferiority failed).
No biopsies were actually withheld, so the study cannot show that deferring a biopsy is safe in routine care.
The cohort had a high share of confirmed significant cancer, limiting how far the savings apply to broader screening.
The Oct 8 release reported no new regulatory decision, orders or sales figure; the Prostate AI had FDA 510(k) clearance and CE marking announced 19 May.
quote_evidence: Those figures describe the combined decision rule, not an AI-only result or an observed reduction in procedures.
No biopsies were actually withheld in the study, so it cannot establish the safety of deferring a procedure in routine care.
why_it_matters_hint: Modelled evidence that AI could trim prostate biopsies, still untested prospectively.
notes: Study dates from 26 Sep; the 8 Oct news is a company release with no new decision or sales data, so score lowered by 1. Article carries stock-price details, omitted.
